core_obligations: Computation of the stalks (proof lines 9433-9443): the author computes the stalk of the pullback at a member of the family by a chain of equalities, using the identification of the pullback with the sheafification of the left Kan extension, the companion result on stalks and the identification of the resulting functor with the given one.

Exactness (proof lines 9444-9448): if each of the given functors defines a point, the composite of the pullback with the corresponding stalk functor is exact, and since the family is conservative the pullback itself is exact, so the functor defines a morphism of sites.
proof_roadmap: Compute the stalks of the pullback at the members of the family.
Use the hypothesis that each functor defines a point to get exactness after taking stalks.
Apply conservativity of the family to conclude exactness.
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a criterion for a continuous functor to define a morphism of sites: it suffices that the composites of the functor with a conservative family of points of the target define points of the source (statement lines 9423-9430). The proof is a complete argument: the stalks of the pullback at the members of the family are computed by a chain of equalities using the companion results (proof lines 9433-9443); the hypothesis then makes the composite of the pullback with each stalk functor exact (proof lines 9444-9445); and conservativity of the family makes the pullback exact, which is the definition of a morphism of sites (proof lines 9446-9448). The non-formal content is the computation of the stalks and the use of conservativity. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
